context: a single passage from a letter by William Whewell, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: I want to be allowed to present the accompanying little book as a marriage gift to you and MrsDarwin. It is a very humble gift, to be sure but it may serve to remind you of my good wishes which are very cordially yours. Moreover if you can accommodate yourself to the canter of the verses, you will find in it a very pretty love story.

I have been very much flattered by your “marriage gift” and kind note. I assure you very few have given me more pleasure.— Mrs. Darwin desires me to give you her best thanks for it.— I hope, sometime when you are in town & happen to be disengaged, we may see you in this house.— I have hardly done more than dip into Herman & D. but I intend beginning it immediately.
